topic: Can satellite orbital configurations optimize ML-based QoS by reducing propagation delays for latency-sensitive traffic classes?
response: Satellite orbital configurations can optimize ML-based QoS by reducing propagation delays for latency-sensitive traffic classes. This can be achieved through the use of lower Earth orbit (LEO) satellites, which have shorter propagation delays compared to geostationary (GEO) satellites. For example, a LEO satellite with an altitude of 1,200 km has a one-way propagation delay of approximately 1.5 ms, whereas a GEO satellite has a one-way propagation delay of around 240 ms. This reduction in propagation delay can be beneficial for latency-sensitive traffic classes, such as real-time video streaming and online gaming.

It emphasizes the need for a proper path selection mechanism that considers the special link characteristics of satellite links, including high fixed latency, to ensure optimal paths for all traffic flows.
